title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list. Compare iterative and recursive merge strategies.

data.text: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists `list1` and `list2`. Merge the two lists into one sorted list. The list should be made by splicing together the nodes of the first two lists.
Use a dummy head node to simplify edge cases. At each step, attach the smaller node and advance that list.

data.title: Iterative O(n + m) — Clean
Dummy node pattern
data.text: The dummy node eliminates special handling for the head. We always build from `dummy.Next` and return `dummy.Next` at the end. This is a recurring pattern in linked list problems.
Recursion naturally handles the merge: pick the smaller head, recursively merge the rest, and attach.

data.title: Recursive O(n + m) time and space
What improved?
data.text: The recursive version is more concise and eliminates the `tail` pointer and `while` loop. However, it uses O(n+m) call stack space. Both are O(n+m) time since we touch each node once.
